lessonTitle: Teamwork and Project Planning: Tasks, Gantt Charts, Roles and Meeting Logs

blocks.text: In week nine of a ten-week project a team discovers that nobody has ordered the aluminium bar. Everyone assumed someone else was doing it. The drawings are perfect, the bar takes five days to arrive, and there are five days left. A task list with a name and a date beside every task would have shown the gap in week one.

blocks.markdown: A team project needs three things: a plan that shows what has to be done and when, roles that show who is responsible, and a record of decisions so the team does not repeat discussions. All three are simple tools. Their value lies in being specific.

blocks.title: Work breakdown and Gantt chart
blocks.text: A **work breakdown** divides the project into tasks small enough to estimate, assign and check. Each task has a name, a duration, an owner and its predecessors. A **Gantt chart** draws each task as a horizontal bar on a time axis, so start, finish and overlaps are visible. Arrows show dependencies, and the longest chain of dependent tasks is the **critical path**.

blocks.markdown: A good task is specific, has one owner and a finishing criterion: 'Machine base plate to drawing 05 (owner: Sam, 2 days)' rather than 'do the build'. Estimate the time as effort divided by the people working and their availability.

blocks.caption: Duration t of a task from effort E (person-days), number of people n and availability a (fraction of a working day actually spent on the task).

blocks.title: Effort to duration
blocks.prompt: Detail design needs 18 person-days of effort. Three team members will work on it, each able to spend 75 % of their time on it. How long will the task take?

steps.text: Express the availability as a fraction: a = 0.75.
Effective person-days per day: n a = 3 x 0.75 = 2.25.
Duration: effort divided by that: 18/2.25 = 8 days.

blocks.answer: Detail design is planned as 8 working days; if one person leaves, it becomes 12 days.

blocks.caption: Task list for a seed-drill prototype project (durations in working days).

blocks.title: Critical path and float
blocks.prompt: Using the task table, find the project duration, the critical path and the float on task G.

steps.text: Forward pass (earliest finish): A 3, B 7, C 13, D 15, E 20, F 23. G starts after C and ends at 13+5 = 18.
Task H needs both F and G, so it starts at the later finish, 23, and ends at 25.
The path A-B-C-D-E-F-H takes 3+4+6+2+5+3+2 = 25 days. It has no spare time, so it is the critical path.
steps.latex: \text{critical path: A, B, C, D, E, F, H}

steps.text: Task G could finish by day 23 (when H needs it) but is planned to finish at 18, so its float is 23 - 18 = 5 days.

blocks.answer: The project takes 25 days. G has 5 days of float; any delay on a critical task delays the whole project.

blocks.markdown: **Roles and milestones.** Assign each team member a clear role, for example coordinator (agenda, chasing progress), design lead, manufacturing lead, test lead and secretary (minutes). Roles do not mean working alone; they mean someone is accountable. Each **milestone** is a checkpoint with a date, a named deliverable and an acceptance criterion.

rows: Specification document with numbered, measurable requirements
Drawing pack and bill of materials
All requirements marked pass or fail
blocks.caption: Example milestone plan.

blocks.title: One owner per task
blocks.text: Shared ownership means no ownership. Give every task and deliverable a single named owner, even when several people help. Review ownership at each meeting.

blocks.markdown: **Meeting records.** A meeting log is a short record of decisions and actions, not a transcript. It states the date, attendees and apologies, each **decision**, and each **action** with an owner and a due date, plus the next meeting date. It is circulated soon after the meeting so errors are corrected while memories are fresh.

items: Decisions: what was agreed, in one line each, with the reason if it matters later.
Actions: what, who and by when (for example 'Order 20 mm bar - Priya - Friday').
Next meeting: date, time and agenda items.

blocks.title: Vague actions do not get done
blocks.text: An action such as 'look into materials' has no owner, no output and no date. Rewrite it as 'Priya to compare three aluminium alloys and report to the team by Thursday'.

points: A work breakdown gives specific tasks with duration, owner and predecessors; a Gantt chart shows them against time, and the critical path is the longest chain of dependent tasks.
Roles make someone accountable, and each milestone needs a date, a named deliverable and an acceptance criterion.
Meeting logs record decisions and actions with owners and due dates, in a concise form circulated promptly.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best-defined task in a project plan?

options.text: Machine the base plate to drawing 05: owner Sam, 2 days, after stock arrives
Do the build
Work on the mechanism
Make progress on the report

questions.correctOptionText: Machine the base plate to drawing 05: owner Sam, 2 days, after stock arrives

distractorRationale.b: No owner, duration or finishing criterion.
distractorRationale.c: Too vague to estimate or check.

questions.explanation: A good task has a specific output, a single owner, an estimated duration and a stated dependency. The vague entries cannot be scheduled or checked.

questions.stem: On a Gantt chart with dependency links, which tasks form the critical path?

options.text: The longest chain of dependent tasks, which have zero float
The tasks with the shortest durations
The tasks owned by the team leader
All tasks that start in the first week

questions.correctOptionText: The longest chain of dependent tasks, which have zero float

distractorRationale.b: Short tasks can have large float and are not critical.
distractorRationale.c: Ownership has no bearing on the critical path.
distractorRationale.d: Start week does not determine criticality.

questions.explanation: The critical path is the longest chain of dependent tasks and sets the minimum project duration. A delay on any task in it delays the whole project, because it has no float.

options.text: Detail design review in week 6: drawing pack checked against the specification and accepted by the supervisor
The team should be about half done by week 6
Design finished around the middle of the project
Work on drawings continues until done

questions.correctOptionText: Detail design review in week 6: drawing pack checked against the specification and accepted by the supervisor

distractorRationale.b: No deliverable and no acceptance criterion.
distractorRationale.d: This is an activity without a checkpoint.

questions.explanation: A milestone is a date with a named deliverable and an acceptance criterion so that everyone can tell whether it has been reached. The weaker statements describe vague progress.

questions.stem: Four members are all listed as 'responsible for testing' with no single owner. What is the most likely consequence and best correction?

options.text: Nobody is clearly accountable, so assign one test lead with the others supporting
Testing will be done faster, so no change is needed
The critical path will shorten automatically
The task should be deleted

questions.correctOptionText: Nobody is clearly accountable, so assign one test lead with the others supporting

distractorRationale.b: Shared responsibility usually leads to gaps and duplication.
distractorRationale.c: Ownership does not alter the logical dependencies.
distractorRationale.d: Testing is needed to verify the design.

questions.explanation: Accountability needs a single named owner, even if several people work on the task. Without it the work is assumed to be someone else's.

questions.stem: Which entry is the best action in a meeting log?

options.text: Order 20 mm aluminium bar from the stores: Priya, by Friday
Look into materials
Someone should check the stock
We discussed ordering stock

questions.correctOptionText: Order 20 mm aluminium bar from the stores: Priya, by Friday

distractorRationale.d: This records discussion, not an action.

questions.explanation: An action states what is to be done, who will do it and by when. Anything missing makes it likely to be forgotten or argued over later.

questions.stem: A project has tasks P1 (2 days, no predecessor), P2 (5 days, after P1), P3 (6 days, after P1), P4 (4 days, after P2 and P3) and P5 (3 days, after P4). What is the minimum project duration in days?
questions.explanation: The path P1-P3-P4-P5 takes $2+6+4+3=15$ days, and P1-P2-P4-P5 takes 14 days. The longest chain sets the duration, so the project takes 15 days.

questions.stem: In the same project (P1 2 days; P2 5 days; P3 6 days; P4 4 days; P5 3 days with P4 after P2 and P3), how many days of float does task P2 have?
questions.explanation: P2 can finish at day 7, but P4 cannot start until P3 finishes at day 8, so P2 could be delayed by $8-7=1$ day. Its float is 1 day, and P3 is on the critical path with zero float.

questions.stem: A task needs 21 person-days of effort. Three people will work on it and each can give 70 % of their time. How many working days will it take?
questions.explanation: Effective capacity is $3\times0.7=2.1$ person-days per day. The duration is $21/2.1=10$ days.

questions.stem: A team of four students has 8 weeks to design and build a bridge load tester. List at least six tasks with durations and predecessors, identify the critical path and explain how a Gantt chart would help the team.
markingGuide: At least six specific tasks with durations and named predecessors
Logical order, such as specification, concepts, detail design, stock order, build, test, report
Critical path identified as the longest dependent chain and its total duration
Shows that parallel tasks (for example report drafting) have float
Gantt chart shows start, finish, overlaps and dependencies, helping to spot delays and resource clashes
questions.explanation: A good answer breaks the project into specific tasks, calculates the critical path from durations and dependencies, and notes where there is float. The Gantt chart is a visual tool for monitoring progress against the plan.

questions.stem: At a team meeting about a prototype pump, the team spent a long time debating three impeller designs, agreed to build design 2 because it was the cheapest and easiest to machine, decided to meet again on Tuesday at 10:00, and Amir will order the stock by Friday while Lena finishes the drawings by Monday. Write the meeting log entries for decisions and actions, and state the roles that make the log useful.
markingGuide: Decision recorded in one line: build impeller design 2, with the reason (lowest cost, easiest to machine)
Action: Amir to order stock by Friday
Action: Lena to finish drawings by Monday
Notes that a secretary records the log and the coordinator checks actions, with no transcript of the debate
questions.explanation: A meeting log records decisions and actions with owners and dates, not the discussion. The roles of secretary and coordinator ensure the log is written and the actions are followed up.
